text:
Ivy (Design): dropped a short prototype GIF showing a "scanline" highlight that tracks across the run history list when you hover a call, dimming unrelated rows. https://figma.com/file/scanline (preview)
Ivy (Design): goal: help users visually connect a tool call in the transcript with its entry in run history without expanding everything.
Sam (DevEx): love that. we get many support threads where users ask which call produced a given CSV. a visual link would reduce confusion.
Diego (Frontend): implementation thoughts: CSS overlay with pointer-events:none for visual line; add data-call-id attributes. keyboard users: need a way to jump the scanline — propose shortcuts: ] and [ to go next/prev call.
Leah (A11y): keyboard nav is key. ensure shortcuts are discoverable (Help menu) and can be disabled. for screen readers the hover-only scanline is invisible so we must also expose a focus state that announces "Selected call: excel_extract, table, 3 rows" using aria-live=polite.
Ravi (QA): test cases: hover highlight, keyboard next/prev, focus announcement content, focus order when jumping, and interaction with virtualized list.
Ivy (Design): micro-copy: when scanline selects a row announce: "Call selected: excel_extract — table — 3 rows". also show a small transient label near the scanline with tool icon + friendly name.
Sam (DevEx): telemetry: record `scanline_hover`, `scanline_keyboard_navigate`, and `scanline_open_details`. add a low-sample rate for hover events to avoid noise.
Diego (Frontend): concern: virtualized lists may re-render and lose the scanline position. plan: persist selected call id in state and scrollIntoView on nav. ETA: ~4 dev days to handle virtualization + a11y.
Leah (A11y): focus behavior: when user uses shortcut to jump, move DOM focus to the summary button inside that row and set aria-describedby to a hidden live region summarizing the structured output. avoid modal traps.
Ivy (Design): visual fallback for crowded lists: if many calls are in view, show a subtle numbered pill on each row so users can use numeric shortcuts too (e.g., press 5 to select the fifth visible call). optional.
Diego (Frontend): numeric shortcuts are doable but need to be disabled when typing in inputs. keyboard manager must ignore when focus is in textareas.
Ravi (QA): add tests for numeric shortcuts, ensure no collisions with browser defaults, and validate screen reader phrasing on NVDA/VoiceOver.
metrics-bot: suggested event schema posted: `scanline_event { type, call_id, user_action, source }`
Sam (DevEx): UX nit: when scanline lands on a call that has no structured metadata (legacy), show a gray badge "legacy" and announce "no structured output available".
Ivy (Design): I'll create two mocks: hover-driven scanline and keyboard-first flow with visible pill. will run quick hallway test tomorrow.
Diego (Frontend): I'll prototype PR branch `devex/scanline-nav` after mocks land. will ping Leah for pair review on a11y.
Leah (A11y): will own the accessibility checklist. pairing with Diego during implementation.
Ravi (QA): I'll add automated e2e tests in Cypress for keyboard flows and aXe checks for the highlighted state.
Ivy (Design): quick poll: react :thumbsup: if you prefer keyboard-first (shortcuts + pills), :eyes: if hover-first (visual scanline) is better.
Sam (DevEx): :thumbsup: (keyboard-first)
Diego (Frontend): :thumbsup: (keyboard-first)
Leah (A11y): :thumbsup:
Ravi (QA): :eyes: (lean hover for discovery, but will test both)
Ivy (Design): thanks all — will upload mocks + tiny script for hallway testing and tag QA + a11y.
